interaction-patterns.summary: In revision 2026-07-28 servers never send JSON-RPC requests. When a tool, prompt or resource read needs user input, a model completion or roots, the server returns an InputRequiredResult and the client retries the original request with the answers. Know the multi round-trip request (MRTR) rules and requestState security, the elicitation modes and their safety rules, the deprecated Sampling and Roots features, subscriptions/listen, the Tasks extension and how extensions are negotiated.
points: MRTR: a server MAY answer `tools/call`, `prompts/get` or `resources/read` (and no other request) with `resultType: "input_required"`, plus `inputRequests` (a map of `elicitation/create`, `sampling/createMessage` or `roots/list` requests) and/or an opaque `requestState`. It MUST include at least one of the two. Every ordinary result carries `resultType: "complete"`.

The retry is an independent request: it MUST use a new JSON-RPC id, MUST echo `requestState` exactly (and MUST NOT include one if none was given), and carries `inputResponses` keyed by the server's `inputRequests` keys. Neither field may be reused on other requests, including parallel ones. Because the server holds no pending state, any replica can handle the retry.

`requestState` is attacker-controlled. If it affects authorization, resource access or business logic it MUST be integrity-protected (HMAC or AEAD) and rejected when verification fails. Servers SHOULD bind the authenticated principal, a short expiry and the originating request (method plus a digest of its parameters). At-most-once use (for example coupon redemption) MUST still be enforced server-side. Use AEAD when the contents must stay secret.

MRTR edge cases: if needed input is missing, the server SHOULD re-ask with a new InputRequiredResult rather than error. Unknown extra keys SHOULD be ignored. Servers MUST NOT assume the client will fulfil the request or retry, and MUST NOT ask for features the client did not declare in that request's `clientCapabilities`.

Elicitation form mode uses a flat object schema with primitive properties only: string (formats `email`, `uri`, `date`, `date-time`), number or integer, boolean, and single- or multi-select enums. No nested objects and no arrays of objects. An empty `elicitation: {}` capability means form mode only.

Servers MUST NOT use form mode for passwords, API keys, access tokens or payment credentials. They MUST use URL mode, where the data never passes through the client. `accept` in URL mode means only consent to open the URL. The server learns the outcome on the retry, from `requestState` or its own stored state, because `notifications/elicitation/complete` and `elicitationId` were removed.

URL-mode client rules: never pre-fetch the URL or its metadata, never open it without consent, show the full URL first, and open it so that neither client nor LLM can see the page (a system browser sheet, not an embedded web view). Servers MUST NOT put credentials or PII in the URL or use pre-authenticated URLs, and MUST check that the user who opens the URL is the one who triggered it (phishing defence).

Third-party OAuth through URL mode makes the server an OAuth client. Third-party tokens MUST NOT transit the MCP client (not even encrypted inside `requestState`), so the server must store them bound to the user's identity. It must never pass through the client's MCP token. Response actions are `accept`, `decline` (an explicit no) and `cancel` (dismissed).

Sampling (deprecated in 2026-07-28; migrate to direct LLM-provider APIs) lets a server borrow the client's model. `modelPreferences` holds cost, speed and intelligence priorities (0 to 1) plus advisory substring `hints`, and the client makes the final choice. `maxTokens` is required and MUST be respected. Tool loops need `sampling.tools`, tool-result-only user messages and a result for every tool use. `toolChoice` is `auto`, `required` or `none`. The `includeContext` values `thisServer` and `allServers` are deprecated.

Roots (deprecated; migrate to tool parameters, resource URIs or server configuration) are `file://` URIs that are informational only and never enforced. `notifications/roots/list_changed` was removed. While roots last, they travel inside an InputRequiredResult as `roots/list`.

`subscriptions/listen` replaced `resources/subscribe`/`unsubscribe` and the HTTP GET stream. The client opts in to `toolsListChanged`, `promptsListChanged`, `resourcesListChanged` or `resourceSubscriptions`. The first message MUST be `notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged`, listing the honoured subset. Every notification carries `io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId`, which equals the listen request's JSON-RPC id. A graceful end is a `complete` response to the listen request. Progress and log notifications stay on their own request's stream.

The Tasks extension (`io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks`) is negotiated per request. The server returns `resultType: "task"` with `taskId`, `ttlMs` and `pollIntervalMs`, durably created first. The client polls `tasks/get`, answers `input_required` with `tasks/update`, and may send `tasks/cancel` (cooperative). There is no `tasks/list` or `tasks/result`. `completed`, `failed` and `cancelled` are terminal. Extensions are opt-in: clients declare them in `clientCapabilities.extensions`, servers in `server/discover`, and the supporting side falls back gracefully (MCP Apps tools still return text).
traps: Saying a 2026-07-28 server sends `elicitation/create` or `sampling/createMessage` as its own JSON-RPC request. Servers MUST NOT initiate requests; everything rides inside an InputRequiredResult.
Retrying with the same JSON-RPC id, or reusing an old `requestState` on a round that did not send one.
Trusting `requestState` because clients MUST NOT modify it. A malicious client can, so integrity protection is required, and base64 is not confidentiality.
Collecting an API key or password with a form-mode field, or putting a clickable link in a form message to dodge URL-mode consent.
Reading URL-mode `accept` as proof that the out-of-band flow succeeded.
Treating roots as a sandbox, or claiming Sampling and Roots were removed. They are deprecated and still work during the window (earliest removal: the first revision on or after 2027-07-28).
Expecting `Last-Event-ID` replay after a dropped listen stream. Resumability is gone, so re-subscribe and re-fetch.
Assuming `tasks/cancel` guarantees a `cancelled` status. Cancellation is cooperative, and a task may still complete.
